observable_features: Separate curved plywood back and seat panels provide broad contact surfaces above a slender metal frame.
Rounded panel corners and a dished seat contrast with the slender round metal supports.
The seat/back separation and open space below the seat keep the structure visually light.
Four splayed metal legs and a narrow back support distribute support without a solid wooden enclosure.

association_evidence.supports: Saint Louis Art Museum identifies its Lounge Chair Metal (LCM), designed in 1946 by Charles Eames and Ray Kaiser Eames, made by the Molded Plywood Division of Evans Products Company, in molded plywood and steel, accession 127:1984.

MoMA documents the same 1946 LCM design and explains its separate molded panels. MoMA’s own physical example, accession 156.1973, is manufactured by Herman Miller and uses molded walnut-veneered plywood, chrome-plated steel rods and rubber shock mounts. Those physical-object details must not be reassigned to the SLAM example.
